requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. I did not read `source_input`, `insert_selector` or `generated_evidence_selector`. I relied on what the tests assert about their output.

**Obligation:** when authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST be in the mandatory input set.

**Implementation:** `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` (lines 65–252) carries it out.
- It seeds `selectors` with `InputSelector::Requirements { requirements: subject_name }` before any other contribution.
- It turns each selector into a mandatory input through `source_input`.
- The subject is never a generated-evidence selector, so the later omission filter does not drop it.
- The `{impl}` marker for `requirements.authoring_input` sits on this function.

**Tests:**
- `unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment` asserts that the mandatory inputs equal exactly one requirement input. It contains the whole declaration, including the opening `:::{req} ready` and closing `:::` fences. This checks the "complete fenced declaration" wording directly. It carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring_input`.
- `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs` asserts that the first input is the full fenced declaration, even when the declaration carries `:impl:` and `:test:` option lines. It also carries a `{test}` reference.
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` checks the example subject's own declaration and carries a `{test}` reference.

The mandatory-input construction itself is covered by the cited `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, so it is not reassessed here.

**Marking and unspecified behavior:** I found no unmarked implementation or tests, and no unspecified behavior.

the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied

be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
